Words used here

Canonical: original working copy. Mirror: preserved notebook copy. Lineage: files used to build a report. Regeneration: rebuilding a page from its preserved inputs. MiB: 1,048,576 bytes. SHA-256: a content checksum. FROZEN: handoff whose transcript cannot be checked here. origin/main: the remote repository branch.

## Short version

Created a standalone HTML teaching page connecting attention, cached keys and values, visibility rules, and work grouping in TRON (the hardware inference system). Its interactive examples and timings are mock data. The transcript records 18 passing browser checks, followed by checks of the final layout at three screen widths.

## Objective

Follow `input-2-ai/internalize-concepts.md` to explain how five concepts relate: attention, KV cache pages (storage blocks for keys and values), sliding windows, visible K/V ranges, and minibatches (groups of token jobs). Include a concept table, parent concepts, diagrams, animations, mock data, and the original prompt.

## Environment

- Work ran on `claude-agentsrv` in `/home/jhan/workspace/random`, using Linux, Bash, and Python 3. This workspace is not a Git repository.
- The local TRON source was `/home/jhan/workspace/tron`. The page pins its source links to commit `9b11a912baa0e5b191ea6f57230c95c224a9c556` on `main`.
- Browser checks used Playwright (browser automation) from `/tmp/amx-browser-py`, Chromium from `/tmp/amx-browsers`, and libraries under `/tmp/amx-browser-libs`. All these paths are on `claude-agentsrv`.
- No inference benchmark or hardware campaign ran in this chat.

## Timeline

- **2026-09-19, 12:21–12:23 PDT:** read the brief and local development instructions. Located the TRON checkout and consulted the PagedAttention and Mistral 7B papers. The design separated query visibility from page storage and minibatch grouping. [Transcript lines 13–89.]
- **12:36–12:41 PDT:** authored the page, embedded the exact brief, and added source links pinned to the TRON commit. Corrected the execution explanation to distinguish ready cache pages from pages waiting for new K/V. Added a diagram showing overlap between accelerator work and CPU attention. [Transcript lines 96–197.]
- **12:43–12:44 PDT:** completed browser checks and plain-English edits. Simplified mobile controls and added horizontal-scroll hints. Rechecked the final page at 1440 px, 390 px, and 320 px viewport widths. [Transcript lines 220–265.]

Includes inline styling, JavaScript, diagrams, source links, and the original prompt. It was authored directly in this chat. There is no external numerical input file or report generator. (preserved: `artifacts/tron/random/TRON-concepts-codex.html`).

- `claude-agentsrv:/home/jhan/workspace/tron` — source checkout used for definitions. The exact version is [TRON commit 9b11a912baa0e5b191ea6f57230c95c224a9c556](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/tree/9b11a912baa0e5b191ea6f57230c95c224a9c556). This chat made no TRON code changes.

## Current state

- The page is complete. Its default mock example has query positions 8–11 and a window of six tokens. Query 11 sees six key positions. The four-query group needs nine distinct key positions across three mock pages. These counts were checked in the browser. [Transcript lines 189–191, 220–233.]
- Changing the mock page capacity changes storage grouping without changing allowed query–key pairs. The validator also checked causality, sequence boundaries, animation controls, and presets. [Transcript lines 220–233.]
- The browser checks confirmed the original prompt was embedded exactly, local anchors resolved, and no external scripts or style sheets were required. The layout stayed light and avoided page overflow at 1440 px, 768 px, 390 px, and 320 px widths, with details both collapsed and expanded. [Transcript lines 220–233.]
- A final check after mobile-label edits passed at 1440 px, 390 px, and 320 px. It checked overflow, the embedded prompt, and the default six-key result. The complete 18-check suite preceded these final presentation edits. [Transcript lines 249–253.]

## Open items / next steps

- User review of the completed page remains the next step. No further implementation was requested after delivery.
- Preserve the authored page and useful validation files through the handoff approval process. Reuse the existing preserved brief.

## Gotchas & decisions

- All animation durations are invented teaching values. They are neither measurements nor performance estimates. The page therefore has no measurement-data lineage to backfill.
- Page boundaries do not determine visibility. Excluding a token from a window does not itself delete its cached K/V.
- Attention on ready pages can begin after the query vector is available. Attention on pending pages waits for the required new K/V. The page's timing diagram deliberately simplifies that overlap.
- The first sandboxed browser attempt stalled. A later run outside the sandbox produced the recorded checks. The transcript's process cleanup found that the earlier process had already exited. [Transcript lines 118–208.]
- The validator uses absolute local paths and the temporary browser installation. Inspect those dependencies before rerunning it on another host.

The source material includes the [PagedAttention paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180) and [Mistral 7B, section 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06825v1#S2). The page distinguishes their general explanations from its pinned TRON source evidence.

Words used here:
- tron: the inference program under test (repo positron-ai/tron). runtron: its command-line tool that loads a model and generates text for N simulated users. rinzler: the serving daemon built from the same tree (systemd units rinzler@0..3 on delphi-3bda).
- AMX: Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, tile matrix instructions used by the new CPU attention kernels. AVX: the older vector instruction set that the code falls back to. "AMX-off" = same binary with the kill switch TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1; "AMX-on" = kill switch unset.
- PR #3879: https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/3879, the AMX attention change. jhan-amx-p0: its branch. 47f6f2dceb: the branch head that was built and measured.
- tp2 / tp4: tensor-parallel degree, how many FPGA cards one model instance spans. qwen: the model ingested-qwen-3-4b-instruct-2507 (tp2 and tp4 variants).
- TPS: decode tokens per second per user. TTFT: time to first token (for runtron, the "Parsing the prompt took" time; for the CI harness, its ttft_ms field).
- CI harness: the throughput benchmark of the nightly System CI (repo positron-ai/systems_test, scripts/perf.py, run here through exec/more-testing-r1/st_perf.py against one engine). Nightly: the scheduled System CI run on delphi-3bda (workflow system_ci_granite_rapids_72_rinzler_OCI).
- CI lease: the file /run/lock/systems-test-ci.lease on delphi-3bda that the nightly holds while it owns the machine. "Our half": socket 1 of delphi-3bda (FPGA instances 2 and 4), the half jhan may use; the other half is shared with Bill.
- Hugepages: 1 GiB pages under /dev/hugepages that model slices are mapped into; 512 exist on delphi-3bda.
- USE_HW_ATTN=0: environment variable that forces attention onto the CPU instead of the FPGA; AMX can only engage there.
- rep: one repetition of a test cell. Cell: one (test, tp, arm) combination.

Words used here:

- tron: the inference server code base at https://github.com/positron-ai/tron. rinzler is its FUSE-based statistics file system.
- AMX: Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile-matrix instructions on Granite Rapids Xeons. AVX-512 is the older 512-bit vector instruction set that the default attention path uses.
- PR 3879 (https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/3879): jhan's pull request adding an AMX software-attention path behind the CMake option TRON_AMX_DISPATCH; branch jhan-amx-p0. On 2026-09-08 it was force-pushed to hold only the canonical path. The K mirror (a second copy of the attention keys in the kernel's layout) is parked in an unopened draft; page-share counters became PR 4267 (https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/4267); a memory-order fix became PR 4265 (https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/4265). Both merged on 2026-09-10.
- Heads: 60d66d9c04 is the pre-split commit the reviewers commented on. 26a0338c3b was the PR head when this session started. 524c510609 was the head after jhan's evening pushes from another session. 4290402491 is the head this session pushed.
- Reviewers: Ben (CHANGES_REQUESTED review, seven open inline threads), Jeremy (one inline thread, written with Codex), Wade (a PR-level evaluation comment with Blocking, Should fix, and Minor sections). Bill approved the PR the same evening from another session.
- Review thread: a GitHub inline comment conversation on a PR file line. Threads are "resolved" by the author when settled.
- apply_page_range, apply_page_tok, apply_dense_amx_page: functions in `h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp`. The first walks the KV-cache pages for one query group; the second handles one page on the AVX path; the third handles a dense page with the AMX kernels.
- Packed Q, the pack: the query block re-laid into the AMX tile layout once per call. attn_accum: the per-thread scratchpad struct that now holds the packed-Q buffer (moved out of a thread_local in commit 752e9f571a).
- range_hint: a token-index hint returned by the page walk to let the caller skip pages. s_pages: a 4-by-64 float score tensor the AMX kernels read as one block.
- Tile region: the span between begin_region() (configure AMX tiles) and end_region() (release them). tron::finally: a scope-guard type in `h/common/util.hpp` that runs a callable at scope exit.
- delphi-3bda: the Granite Rapids test machine with AMX. Its nightly system CI prep window began at 02:45 UTC on 2026-09-11. delphi-3af6: the GitHub Actions test host that ran the last green CI run.
- split-verify3.sh: the project's build-and-test script in `~/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/`, launched on delphi-3bda with a lease and lock guard from `lib-guard.sh`.
- Workflow: a background multi-agent verification run inside Claude Code (this session used five).
- est.: an estimate, not a measurement.

Page-share counters became PR 4267 (https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/4267), and a memory-order fix became PR 4265 (https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/4265); both merged on 2026-09-10.
- Old head 60d66d9c04: the pre-split commit that Bill's review examined. 524c510609: the PR head Bill approved on 2026-09-10. 4290402491 and 47f6f2dceb: later PR heads pushed during this evening (see Timeline).
- Bill's findings: a Claude-generated architecture review titled "AMX Review Findings" (14 findings, dated 2026-09-05), which Bill linked from their approval of PR 3879. jhan saved it locally as `Bill-claude-AMX Review Findings.html`. A companion artifact "AMX Backend Seam" proposes a backend struct type for the kernel entry points.
- CI: the GitHub Actions workflows of tron. "CMake and CTest" is the workflow that builds and runs the unit tests. Issue 3997 (https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/issues/3997) tracks making one real-AMX test execution a required check.
- Test fakes: t_amx_dispatch_dtype defines stand-in kernel functions in the test's own object so the test links without the real AMX kernel object.
- ODR: the C++ One Definition Rule. LTO / ThinLTO: link-time optimization. lld: the LLVM linker.
- Artifact: a private web page published from Claude Code at claude.ai.
- Workflow: a background multi-agent verification run inside Claude Code (this session used three).
- R1-47: an entry in the project's triage file `triage.json` recording an earlier reviewer decision that the CPU probe stays in the kernel translation unit.

# Handoff: range_hint audit for PR #3879 answers Ben's question (AMX path needs no hint handling); reviews/range_hint.html written; two comment-only commits pushed (339dde7fe7, 524c510609)

> Generated by Claude (Claude Code) on 2026-09-11.

- Activity dates: 2026-09-10
  (source: transcript timestamps)
- Claude session: "range_hint handling in tron PR 3879"
  (project: /home/jhan/workspace/intel-AMX/PR3879/new-PRs/PR1)
  - Transcript: claude-agentsrv:/home/jhan/.claude/projects/-home-jhan-workspace-intel-AMX-PR3879-new-PRs-PR1/4522d927-a06a-4a4b-9642-e7b1bb418a38.jsonl

Words used here:

- **tron**: Positron's inference server code base (GitHub repo positron-ai/tron).
- **PR #3879 / PR1**: https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/3879, branch `jhan-amx-p0`, "AMX software attention, canonical path: kernel + dispatch, default-off".
- **AMX**: Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (tile-matrix instructions). **AVX-512 dotter loop** (or "the dotter"): the existing per-entry attention loop in `h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp` that the AMX path replaces for some pages.
- **KV page / page**: 64 consecutive stored key/value tokens. **dense page**: a page where the whole 64-token page is active, visible to the query through one range, and inside the query's sliding window. Only dense pages take the AMX path; the test is `is_dense_amx_page`.
- **ranged mask**: the per-forward-pass table of token ranges (`token_range`, fields `tok_lo`, `tok_hi`, plus a software mask and a hardware mask) that says which query tokens may see which stored tokens. Defined in `h/tron/models/ranged_mask.hpp` and `src/tron/models/ranged_mask.cpp`.
- **range_hint**: a cached pointer into the ranged mask. `find_range(token, hint)` returns at once when the token lies in the hinted range, walks up to 4 ranges forward otherwise, and falls back to a binary search after that. `apply_page_range` seeds it per page (`page_begin_hint`, `page_end_hint`); `apply_page_tok` advances it inside a page when an entry reaches `tok_hi`.
- **sliding window**: for some model layers a query may attend only to the last W tokens before it (`sliding_window_size`).
- **fence branch**: `jhan-amx-fence`, a measurement branch (worktree /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-fence-amx) carrying `TRON_AMX_FALLBACK_COUNTERS` (commit 3cd2670df1), which counts every page visit that could not take the AMX path, by cause. **range_cut**: the cause "a range boundary falls inside the page".
- **prefill / decode**: prompt processing / token-by-token generation. **TTFT**: time to first token. **TPS**: tokens per second per user.
- **Ben**: the tron reviewer (GitHub login bgamari-positron). **Bill**: the colleague who wrote the ranged mask (history Feb to Mar 2026).
- **Workflow**: a Claude Code multi-agent run that independently read the code, then attacked each claim with three "lenses" and a fresh-eyes bug hunt.
- **claude-agentsrv**: the podman container where this Claude Code ran (called claude-box in the user's docs; host sw-dev-01). /home/jhan is NFS, shared with delphi-3bda.

   3. Executable knowledge or an irreplaceable document: scripts, tools,
-     generators, configs, recipes, analysis/plan docs, distilled-knowledge pages
-     (HTML/md). Litmus test: if the workspace vanished tonight, would
-     recreating this cost hours-to-days?
-  4. Not bulk or regenerable data (benchmark result trees, raw logs, large trace
-     files, turbostat captures, and raw command dumps stay on their storage).
+     generators, configs, recipes, analysis/plan docs, distilled-knowledge
+     pages (HTML/md), or measurement data that a preserved report page,
+     or a handoff's Results table, is computed from (added 2026-09-20).
+     Litmus test: if the workspace vanished tonight, would recreating
+     this cost hours-to-days, or be impossible? Measurement data is the
+     impossible case: a test cannot be re-run into the same numbers once
+     the binary, the machine state and the time are gone.
+  4. Not bulk or regenerable data. Judge each file by its class and its
+     size, never by its location: a file is not excluded for sitting
+     inside a result tree (updated 2026-09-20: the old wording excluded
+     "benchmark result trees" as a whole).
+     - Classes that stay on their storage: server logs (for example
+       `rinzler.log`, the inference server's log), raw turbostat
+       captures (per-interval output of the Linux CPU power sampler,
+       hundreds of lines or more), campaign logs and `.done` markers,
+       binaries, CI client logs (`perf*.log`) when the sibling
+       `perf*.json` holds the per-request samples, and per-repetition
+       logs when a proposed compact result text already holds the lines
+       that carry the page's measured numbers (check those lines one by
+       one, not by appearance). One override: a file that the page, its
+       input, or the handoff's Results table takes a measured number
+       from (a rate, a time, a power reading) is a source and is
+       proposed, whatever its class, unless a proposed compact text
+       holds every such line. A line citation in the input is the usual
+       evidence, and for an authored page the `sources:` label is
+       enough. Lines used for identity or configuration (version,
+       commit, device count, NUMA node, memory footprint) do not trigger
+       it.
+     - Size: a single file above 5 MiB (5242880 bytes) is not proposed.
+       List it at the gate as `left behind (size)` with its byte count,
+       and I can approve it there. State every batch's file count and
+       total MiB at the gate, plus the clone's `.git` size from `du -sm`
+       or a native disk-usage equivalent reporting MiB.
+     - Regenerable means a command rebuilds the file from files already
+       in git. A file that can only be rebuilt from unpreserved data, a
+       hand-edited file, or a file a Workflow built (agent steps, not

 ## Current state
 
 The completed report concludes that **a single persistent swizzled CPU K is technically viable**, with a storage-interface migration and native pagewise AVX readers. FPGA transfers already use a separate GOF shuffle buffer, so direct layout-aware reads can feed the existing hardware format. The mirror’s rationale is migration scope and performance risk, rather than an ISA or FPGA requirement for canonical CPU K.
